text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — proposal to decompose the eviction contract into two orthogonal layers: (1) allocator (global scoring + candidate selection) and (2) owner (local demote/evict ops + correctness). sketch attached, want feedback on tradeoffs.

sam: short q — why split? seems like extra moving parts.

maria: single contract ends up coupling scoring heuristics into owner APIs, which leaks global state. split lets allocator evolve global heuristics (e.g., hotset heatmaps) without forcing owners to know those internals. also reduces surface area for owner implementations (owner just accepts tokens).

jordan: my main worry is correctness: what prevents double-evict or lost-evict when allocator and owner disagree about candidate liveness? need idempotency + reconciliation.

lee: idea for token shape (rough):
```
{
  prefix: "tenant/1234/a",
  lease_epoch: 42,
  action_id: "alloc-2024-09-12T12:34:56Z-0001",
  signature: "sha256(...)"
}
```
owner validates signature + epoch CASes the prefix epoch before mutating. if CAS fails, owner aborts. simple and deterministic.

olivia: +1 to token + CAS. ops angle: we still need safe rollback and observability. recommend a shadow canary (1% of nodes) and a reconciliation job that cross-checks allocator's outstanding tokens with owners.

maria: agreed. rough plan: 1) implement token + owner-side CAS demote, 2) initial step is "soft-demote" (lower priority, no immediate eviction), 3) background reconciler checks for tokens stuck > TTL and triggers stronger actions.

sam: race case: owner acknowledges token (writes pending log), then crashes before demote. allocator thinks owner applied it. how do we detect and fix?

jordan: owner must persist pending-action journal before ack. reconcilers read owner journal + allocator state. if owner journal says pending but no state change after restart and token TTL expired, reconciler can re-enqueue or escalate to emergency reclaim. avoids blind double-apply because actions are idempotent via action_id.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary push scheduled: k8s/evict-decompose/canary v0.1 -> nodeset canary-evict-1 at commit abc1234.

olivia: test plan suggestions: synthetic hotkey workload, inject node crash at ack point, monitor metrics: evict_rate, prefix_misreads, 99th_tail_lat. Also run cross-node read-after-evict regressions.

maria: timeline: I'll prototype token API + owner CAS this week, pair with @jordan on the correctness proof and the reconciler sketch. will post PR when prototype passes basic unit tests.

sam: +1. nit: call the field "lease_epoch" to avoid colliding with other epoch semantics.

jordan: ack. checklist for PR: token shape + signature validation, owner pending-journal persist, CAS demote path, reconcilers + TTL config, canary rollout doc.

maria: thanks — if nobody objects I'll fold this into the RFC follow-up doc and open the prototype PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

lee: yeah looks good, curious to see perf impact of soft-demote.

olivia: please add SLOs to the rollout doc (evict correctness SLA + remediation SOP).

maria: will do, thanks everyone.
